title: Squad-to-battalion small-UAS fleet control, registry, deconfliction, tasking and collection forwarding for Drone Dominance mass (multi-vendor drones into company/battalion C2, S2 and training pipelines)

scores.rationale: FACT/HIGH: units hand-mark drone positions (BARS) and run procedural deconfliction because tracks do not populate the COP (3rd CAB pre-JMRC plan; CALL 25-14, army.mil, 2025-09), and 2-35 IN reports a doctrine/tooling gap at JPMRC 26-01 (Small Wars Journal, 2026-09-16); but the Army has judged the pain tolerable via procedure, so it is a real but coped-with pain, not a mission-stopping one.

FACT/HIGH: the pain recurs on every flight in every company/battalion receiving Gauntlet/SRR drones (12,080 accepted, 30,000 inbound, Military Times 2026-09-18), during every CTC rotation and every training event; frequency is the strongest part of the case.

Score of 1 explained: no program element, budget line, RFI or sources-sought for a unit-level sUAS fleet/airspace/collection software layer exists (card budget section, confidence LOW; search log negative). Adjacent money is airframe procurement (SRR/MRR/LRR per CRS IF12668, 2026-05) and an unappropriated FY27 reconciliation request ($53.6B Drone Dominance, Defense Daily 2026) - request is not appropriation, program ceiling is not obligation, and none of it is a software line. Not 0 only because xTech/OTA/CSO discretionary money and unit-level purchase authority exist in principle.

INFERENCE/MEDIUM: the requirement owner (T2COM via MCoE/USAACE) and program office (PEO Aviation PM UAS vs. TAK Product Center vs. RCCTO) are inferred, not identified; the only accessible on-ramps are xTech prizes, TAK.gov plugin submission and a unit-invited CTC trial, none of which is a purchase; the PROBLEM->USER->REQUIREMENT OWNER->PROGRAM OFFICE->CONTRACTING->BUDGET->VEHICLE chain breaks at REQUIREMENT OWNER and again at BUDGET.

FACT/HIGH for the MVP (ATAK-CIV SDK open-sourced per E07; MAVLink/PX4/ArduPilot telemetry self-collectable; CoT is an open schema), but the load-bearing assumption - cross-vendor telemetry from the drones that actually matter (Skydio, Auterion, Gauntlet vendors) without vendor cooperation - is unproven and vendor-gated (card data_requirement), and DDIL networks make any live fleet picture unreliable at company level.

Card estimates PoC at $60k-$120k (fits) but a credible military demo at $400k-$900k and first production deployment at $2M-$5M; $250k covers the PoC and travel to one field trial only if an xTech prize, OTA or vendor partner funds the rest - none secured. Confidence MEDIUM.

A three-drone field demo (CoT tracks, ACM conflict warning, offline ledger sync, clip-to-S2 inbox) is achievable in 3-6 months on commercial hardware; a demo a battalion S3 air would find credible (real vendor feeds, a CTC rotation) needs 9-12 months and a unit sponsor the team does not have. Confidence MEDIUM.

FACT/MEDIUM: PX4/ArduPilot telemetry and synthetic ACOs built from FM 3-52/CALL 25-14 are freely obtainable; but Skydio Cloud API and Auterion CoT need partner access, Gauntlet vendor telemetry formats are not public, real ACOs and unit operator records are CUI reachable only via unit sponsorship, and C-UAS track formats are controlled - the data that makes the product valuable is exactly the data the team cannot get.

Unclassified, software-only MVP on ATAK-CIV and commercial drones is EAR99-level per E07 (describe, do not conclude); burden rises with TAK.gov plugin signing/ATO, CUI handling of ACOs and unit records (NIST 800-171/CMMC), any 9D610-type Gauntlet technical data (BIS deemed-export review for the Indonesian founder - needs counsel), and C-UAS C2 integration. SBIR/STTR closed under 13 CFR 121.702 while both founders are foreign persons (E07, eCFR). Medium burden overall.

FACT/HIGH: ATAK-CIV and SDK are open source (deptofdefense GitHub per E07), PX4/ArduPilot drones are commercial, CoT and MISB KLV are public standards, synthetic airspace data can be built from public doctrine; nothing in the MVP requires a clearance or CUI. Not 5 because the militarily relevant version (real ACOs, Gauntlet telemetry) quickly leaves the unclassified/commercial envelope.

Score of 1 explained (5 = least intense): the seam is crowded on every side - Auterion Nemyx (cross-vendor CoT-to-ATAK, Gauntlet production award; The Defense Post 2025-09-05, vendor claim), AeroVironment/Tomahawk Kinesis (lead SW/systems integrator for HMIF Inc 1, avinc.com 2025-09-29), Anduril Lattice (JIATF-401 C-UAS C2 $87M task order and Army enterprise agreement, DefenseScoop 2026-03-14; multi-vendor tasking/deconfliction marketed - vendor claim), Skydio Cloud for the largest SRR fleet, and a free government-owned TAK UAS Tool plugin (tak.gov, per feasibility skeptic). Not 0 because no one sells a vendor-neutral, unit-owned registry/qualification layer per se.

INFERENCE/MEDIUM: each incumbent is vendor-locked (Auterion covers AuterionOS airframes, Skydio its own, AV its integrations) and the government fusion layer stops at division (TITAN 17 systems, DefenseScoop 2026-09-01), so a vendor-neutral seam exists; but the TAK Product Center and Anduril can each cover it at marginal cost, and vendors can close their APIs to an aggregator, so the vulnerability is narrow and temporary.

FACT/HIGH per card: the startup controls none of the interfaces (TAK/CoT and plugin signing by TAK Product Center; telemetry/API by each drone vendor; C-UAS C2 by JIATF-401/Anduril; TITAN by PEO IEW&S/Palantir); integrating 3-5 Gauntlet/SRR vendors per brigade set is the $2M-$5M cost curve that looks like bespoke systems integration rather than a product.

Score of 1 explained: the card's own defensibility section says none of the proprietary elements (adapters, workflow, footprint, relationships, data) is a hard moat and that TAK PC or Anduril can replicate the workflow; per-airframe registry adds little on expendable one-way-attack drones (the bulk of the mass); realistic barriers are plugin signing/ATO and unit relationships, which are earned, not owned. Not 0 because a CTC-validated, unit-adopted workflow plus vendor adapters would carry some switching cost.

Public-safety DFR programs, wildfire/disaster response and critical-infrastructure operators need the same multi-vendor registry, airspace-check and evidence-forwarding workflow on ATAK-CIV/TAK; but Skydio Cloud, DroneDeploy-type tools and UTM providers already serve them, so dual-use is a proving ground more than a revenue line (card: medium). Confidence MEDIUM.

Expansion paths (blue-drone feed into C-UAS C2, S2 collection indexing, allied armies buying multi-vendor sUAS mass, NATO sensor-agnostic drone C2 ambitions) exist but each runs into the same 'doctrine plus TAK plus vendor OS' substitution and into Ukraine-derived tools already cited by European buyers (card allied_extension); expansion widens the surface without removing the killer risk. Confidence MEDIUM.

A per-battalion subscription or sustainment line is conceivable, but no Army buying pattern for unit-level sUAS software exists today (units buy drones, doctrine is free), and expendable Gauntlet airframes do not create lifecycle-management renewals; realistic recurring revenue is services/support tied to a sponsor unit. Confidence MEDIUM.

The engineer can build ATAK-CIV plugins and MAVLink ingestion today (E07 calls TAK the best immediate fit); but two of three fatal-if-absent roles (former battalion S3 air/UAS master trainer with CTC experience; drone systems engineer with Skydio/Auterion API access) are absent, no unit relationship exists, SBIR is closed to the current cap table (13 CFR 121.702), and the Indonesian founder faces deemed-export exposure once Gauntlet technical data or CUI enters the company (needs counsel). Confidence MEDIUM.

market.summary: No budget owner, program element, RFI or requirement exists for a unit-level sUAS fleet/airspace/collection software layer; the Army's institutional answer (CALL Handbook 25-14, 2025-09) is $0 procedural airspace control designed for the degraded-comms case, TAK is free, TITAN deliberately stops at division (17 systems), Gauntlet mass is expendable one-way-attack drones with low registry value, and the integration cost curve ($60k PoC to $2-5M per brigade set) looks like bespoke systems integration; every seam is already being closed by Auterion, AV/Kinesis, Anduril or Skydio. Narrower version offered: offline-first qualification/training-readiness ledger as a free TAK-CIV plugin monetized via services with one sponsoring battalion/CTC.

competition.summary: Anduril Lattice for Mission Autonomy plus Menace-T/X already markets multi-vendor tasking/route/deconfliction at company-to-brigade echelon (vendor claim) on an awarded Army enterprise vehicle, with Raft contracted for registries/federation inside the NGC2 data layer; TAK/CoT already ingests drone telemetry for free; Skydio can extend Skydio Cloud into its ~60k-drone base; and the Army's residual problem is framed by leadership as training, not a C2 product. Narrower version offered: TAK-native, Lattice/NGC2-compatible training-and-readiness layer sold to schoolhouses/Guard/Reserve, sized as services-adjacent revenue.

feasibility.summary: The government's own free TAK 'UAS Tool' plugin already provides UAS SA/telemetry/FMV/C2 inside ATAK/WinTAK and the same office controls plugin signing; Army common-controller efforts have repeatedly restarted or been cancelled; cross-vendor telemetry from the vendors that matter is API-gated by competitors; SBIR is closed to the current cap table and the militarily useful version (real ACOs, Gauntlet telemetry, C-UAS feed) walks into CUI/9D610 exposure for the Indonesian founder; costs of $400k-$5M exceed $250k by 2-20x with a 5-year path to production as the base case. Narrower version offered: offline registry/qualification ledger plus procedural pre-flight checklist against unit-authored ACMs, acknowledged as small and hard to defend.

verdict_rationale: All three skeptics refute at strength 4 and I concur; the evidence they rely on is tier-1/2 and internally consistent with the gap card, and I found nothing in the research corpus that rebuts it. The decisive reason is the broken demand chain: PROBLEM (real, FACT/HIGH) -> USER (company drone team leads, S3 air, UAS master trainers - real) -> REQUIREMENT OWNER (T2COM/MCoE/USAACE - INFERENCE only; their published answer is CALL 25-14 procedure, army.mil 2025-09) -> PROGRAM OFFICE (none owns a software layer; PM UAS buys airframes, TAK PC ships free plugins) -> CONTRACTING OFFICE (unidentified for a software-only layer) -> BUDGET (none; only unappropriated reconciliation requests and airframe lines, CRS IF12668 2026-05) -> VEHICLE (only xTech prizes/OTAs contingent on a sponsor that does not exist). That is a major-penalty condition under the scoring rules. Three compounding facts make the penalty terminal rather than provisional: (a) the government already gives away the core wedge (TAK UAS Tool plugin, ATAK-CIV open source per E07; CoT tracks are free), so the startup would compete against a $0 government-owned baseline whose owner also controls plugin signing; (b) the vendor-neutral seam depends on telemetry access that the direct competitors (Auterion, Skydio, AV, Gauntlet vendors) control and have every incentive to withhold, while Anduril can expose blue-drone tracks inside Lattice for units already on its Army enterprise agreement (DefenseScoop 2026-03-14); (c) the volume driver is expendable one-way-attack drones (12,080 accepted, 30,000 inbound, Military Times 2026-09-18) where per-airframe registry adds little, and the Army's own fusion layer (TITAN, 17 systems, DefenseScoop 2026-09-01) deliberately stops at division. Absence of a competitor selling exactly this layer is not evidence of opportunity; here it reflects absence of a buyer. On the narrower version all three skeptics converge on (an offline qualification/training-readiness ledger as a TAK-CIV plugin): I judge it a feature or a services engagement, not a company - its buyer is a training-management workflow the Army already runs in its own enterprise training records system (RECALL - not re-verified this session, LOW-MEDIUM), it has no budget line either, and the skeptics themselves concede it 'may not clear the bar for venture-scale outcomes'. It can be a credibility project that opens a TiC battalion door for a different gap, which is why I record it below, but it does not rescue G09 to 'borderline'. Residual uncertainty: a T2COM/PEO Aviation RFI or OTA for a vendor-neutral unit-level sUAS registry/deconfliction layer with named funding, or evidence a battalion paid for such a third-party tool at a CTC, would reopen the question; none exists as of 2026-09-25 (public evidence insufficient for any demand signal in this exact form).
narrower_version_if_borderline: Not applicable (verdict is kill). For the record, the only form that survives at all is the one all three skeptics independently proposed: an offline-first, vendor-agnostic operator/airframe/battery/qualification and training-readiness ledger with a procedural pre-flight check against unit-authored ACMs, shipped as a free ATAK-CIV plugin and paid for (if at all) through a services/integration engagement with one sponsoring Transformation-in-Contact battalion or CTC, explicitly positioned as a complement to CALL 25-14 procedures and to whichever vendor OS/Lattice/Kinesis layer the unit already has. Treat it as a door-opening credibility project (3-4 months, under $60k) that earns a unit relationship and TAK.gov plugin experience reusable on another gap, not as the basis for a company or for raising $2-5M.
most_important_question_answer: If two exceptionally capable founders had $250,000 today and insisted on this gap, the only rational first build is the skeptics' narrow version: a free ATAK-CIV plugin plus a small offline-first edge service that (1) keeps a unit-owned registry of airframes, batteries, operators and qualifications that syncs opportunistically, (2) checks a planned sUAS flight against unit-entered altitude blocks/ROZs/launch points from CALL 25-14 and flags conflicts before launch, and (3) shows any drone that already emits CoT or MAVLink as a blue track - roughly $50-80k and 3-4 months, deliberately avoiding vendor-gated APIs, CUI and C-UAS integration. They would show it to a battalion S3 air NCO and UAS master trainer in a Transformation-in-Contact battalion (2-35 IN / 25th ID or a 4ID/101st unit), to the CTC O/C-T airspace cell that wrote CALL 25-14, and to an xTech panel; the demonstration would prove that the pre-flight check and ledger replace spreadsheet/binder tracking and BARS hand-marking without a network, and the unit would care because it removes real friction from every flight and every readiness report. That is where the case breaks: an incumbent can crush them trivially - the TAK Product Center already ships a free government UAS Tool plugin and controls the signing path the startup must pass through; Auterion, Skydio and AV own the telemetry the product would need to become more than a checklist; and Anduril can expose the same blue-drone view inside Lattice for units already on its Army enterprise agreement - and there is no milestone that unlocks $2-5M because no requirement owner, program office or budget line exists to buy the result. The milestone that would justify a $2-5M raise - a paying battalion or brigade contract, or a T2COM/PEO Aviation RFI or OTA naming a vendor-neutral unit-level sUAS registry/deconfliction layer with funds attached - has no identified owner as of 2026-09-25, so the demo would at best yield an xTech prize or a small services engagement. The founders should treat this as a relationship-building side project and redirect the $250k to a gap where a budget line and a program office already exist.
bear_case_summary: The pain is real but the Army has chosen a $0 answer (CALL 25-14 procedural airspace control plus free TAK/CoT), no requirement, RFI, program office or budget line exists for a unit-level sUAS software layer, TITAN deliberately stops fusion at division, the vendor-neutral seam depends on telemetry APIs that direct competitors (Auterion, Skydio, AV, Gauntlet vendors) control and Anduril can absorb inside Lattice, the government's own TAK UAS Tool plugin already ships free, the mass drones are expendable so registry value is low, the integration cost curve is bespoke systems integration rather than product, and the founding team lacks the fatal-if-absent military airspace/UAS operator, unit access and SBIR eligibility - so the best case is a feature absorbed by a government team or Anduril, not a company.
bull_case_summary: Tens of thousands of multi-vendor drones are reaching squads faster than doctrine and tooling (12,080 Gauntlet accepted, 30,000 inbound, 60,000 expected from Gauntlet 2; 2,500+ X10D), units document hand workarounds (BARS marking, spreadsheets) because tracks do not populate the COP, no vendor is structurally able to be neutral across Auterion/Skydio/AV/Gauntlet ecosystems, TITAN leaves company/battalion without any fusion node, ATAK-CIV and CoT give a free open delivery path with no citizenship test, xTech/OTAs are open to foreign-person founders, allied armies (Germany, UK, Poland, NATO) want sensor-agnostic drone C2, and a team that reached a CTC-validated, unit-adopted workflow first could become the acquisition target of a vendor or the reference for a future T2COM requirement - the bull case is an acquisition or a follow-on requirement, not a standalone revenue line, and it rests on a demand signal that has not yet appeared.
